items.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023
items.q: the Dorsey name was as big as Elvis Presley in terms of the lasting

ctx.x: Do you recall the first time, or a significant time when you witnessed segregation or racial attitudes that were mysterious to you?

I mean yes, but only in those days no. I was really colorblind. But then when I first went with the Dorsey band, which was — this was a hell of a lot later — this would be when I was 20 I went with the Dorsey band and I was going to meet them in Shreveport, Louisiana. And I took the milk plane around to every milk stop around the country to get to Shreveport. Oh my God, and I’d never flown before and I wasn’t ready for it, believe me. No it was not what I wanted, what I wanted to be doing? But I got out in…

and it was the first time you had segregated water, separated bathrooms, separated restaurants. I’d never ever seen that. And we toured the rest of the summer around the south. Back then the Dorsey band was fully booked because the ballrooms in the country were still — they still existed for Christ’s sake. So, and the Dorseys, you’ve got to remember in 1940 the Dorsey name was as big as Elvis Presley in terms of the lasting — they had legs, they had legs.
